title: DMK Targets Tamil Nadu CM Vijay Over Trisha Krishnan's Presence at Independence Day Event
excerpt: The DMK's party mouthpiece called the actress's front-row seat at Fort St George a 'shameless spectacle,' marking the latest chapter in a political feud that has drawn police complaints, arrests, and national attention.
body:
• The DMK's party mouthpiece has attacked Tamil Nadu CM Vijay over actress Trisha Krishnan's front-row presence at the state's Independence Day function at Fort St George on August 15, calling it a 'shameless spectacle.'
  • The criticism is the latest flashpoint in a months-long political feud that previously led to DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin's arrest over remarks linking Vijay and Trisha at a Cauvery water rally.
  • Vijay, who became Chief Minister in May 2026 after TVK won 108 seats in its debut election, ended a nearly six-decade hold on power by Dravidian parties DMK and AIADMK.
  • TVK's women's wing has filed complaints with both police and the National Commission for Women over what it calls the DMK's pattern of targeting a woman public figure.

Tamil Nadu's opposition DMK has intensified its attacks on Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay after actress Trisha Krishnan attended the state's Independence Day celebration at Fort St George in Chennai on August 15. The DMK's party mouthpiece described the event as a "shameless spectacle" and said the "dignity of the Chief Minister has been blown away," according to reports in NDTV and Hindustan Times.

Trisha attended the official function in a traditional yellow saree, which she later revealed on social media belonged to her mother, Uma Krishnan. The DMK's commentary focused on what it characterized as the inappropriateness of a film actress occupying a prominent seat at an official state ceremony.

A Pattern of Escalation

The Independence Day criticism follows a far more explosive confrontation in early August. During a DMK-organized protest rally over the Cauvery water dispute in Thanjavur, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin — the former deputy chief minister and son of ex-CM M.K. Stalin — was addressing the crowd when supporters began chanting "Trisha, Trisha."

https://x.com/TimesNow/status/2089596335813271860

According to Devdiscourse, Stalin paused and allegedly remarked, "Whether the water reaches anywhere else or not, it should reach there," before claiming he was referring to the Cauvery water. TVK's women's wing filed a complaint with the Thanjavur police station, alleging the remark was a "double-entendre" targeting Trisha Krishnan.

"Udhayanidhi Stalin resorted to offensive, double-meaning remarks and vulgar innuendos targeting a prominent female public figure, prompted by an audience chant."

— TVK complaint to the National Commission for Women

An FIR was subsequently filed, and Udhayanidhi was arrested from his Chennai residence. TVK MLA Rhevanth Charan called the remarks "absolutely disgusting" and accused the DMK of "declining standards" in political discourse. The DMK termed the arrest "political vendetta," with party leader TKS Elangovan insisting that Udhayanidhi "didn't even name Trisha."

Cinema, Politics, and Tamil Nadu's New Era

The political weaponization of Vijay's relationship with Trisha — both are among Tamil cinema's biggest names — reflects the unique intersection of film and politics in Tamil Nadu. Vijay, popularly known as 'Thalapathy,' became Chief Minister in May 2026 after his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam party won 108 seats in its debut election, ending the nearly six-decade dominance of the DMK and AIADMK.

Trisha, who starred alongside Vijay in the 2004 blockbuster Ghilli, was seated in the front row at his swearing-in ceremony alongside his parents. She visited his residence on election night as results showed TVK heading toward a historic victory. Their decades-long friendship has been a consistent target for the DMK since losing power.

What's at Stake

For the DMK, now in opposition for the first time in years, the personal attacks on Vijay represent a strategy of delegitimization against a political outsider who shattered their hold on Tamil Nadu. For Vijay's TVK, the response has been institutional — filing police complaints and approaching the NCW rather than engaging in public mudslinging.

The feud shows no signs of cooling. With the state Assembly in session and Vijay still in the early months of his tenure, the DMK's willingness to turn Trisha's public appearances into political ammunition suggests this confrontation will remain a fixture of Tamil Nadu's charged political landscape — and a storyline that the global Tamil diaspora is watching closely.
image_caption: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay and actress Trisha Krishnan have been the focus of political attacks from the opposition DMK. The latest controversy centers on Trisha attending the state Independence Day function at Fort St George.
nri_angle: The escalating political feud between Tamil Nadu's ruling TVK and opposition DMK blends Kollywood stardom with state governance in ways that resonate deeply with the global Tamil diaspora.
